predicate.label: fought military conflict against
predicate.definition: Political entity or military group X fought an armed conflict or war against Y.
includes: explicit war-with or fought-against in an armed-conflict context
actual military attack or combat against Y
excludes: sports competition or metaphorical political attack
cooperation, alliance, or joint action on the same side
border adjacency or diplomatic relations alone
ambiguous: fight-with whose allied versus adversarial sense is unresolved
predicate.notes: Military adversarial conflict is distinct from cooperation and from criticizing. The predicate does not imply a winner.
predicate.scope_notes: Includes: explicit war-with or fought-against in an armed-conflict context; actual military attack or combat against Y; historical military adversaries. Excludes: sports competition or metaphorical political attack; cooperation, alliance, or joint action on the same side; border adjacency or diplomatic relations alone; planned conflict without realization. Ambiguous unless resolved by case-local evidence: fight-with whose allied versus adversarial sense is unresolved; generic attack without military context; future threat or proposed war. Military adversarial conflict is distinct from cooperation and from criticizing. The predicate does not imply a winner.

rationale: Military invasion is the strongest repeated unambiguously interpretable path (two occurrences). Underspecified go/use/ask/summon or roster-trade fragments cannot support an alternative common action; athlete/coach pairs remain outside the warfare scope.
